text:
incident-bot: Pager alert: HIGH_ERROR_RATE on dedicated-pool-us-west-2 (rate > 8% for 5m). Affected route: /v1/generate (customer tier: dedicated). Incident ID: INC-2026-0423

oncall-leah: picking up. looking at graphs now.

omar: I see a spike in 502s and a simultaneous drop in active_workers for that pool. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/p/dedicated/pool-us-west-2

priya: logs show router started rejecting tokens with `variant-compat` errors around 15:02 UTC. sample: `router: variant mismatch: requested "opt-quant-v2" not available, fallback initiated -> 0 backends`

jensen: that error string means fallback policy tried to reroute to compatible variant but there were no healthy backends in the fallback group. could be autoscaler killed instances earlier.

rui: checking autoscaler events... `autoscaler-controller`: scaled_down pool-us-west-2 from 12 -> 3 at 15:01 due to metric "available_capacity" < 0.1 for 3m.

maya: wait, why would available_capacity go negative? that's a derived metric from `gpu_free_slots - reserved_slots` plus a fudge factor. there was a recent metrics rename change rolled last night (`free_slots` -> `gpu_free_slots`) — maybe router/AS reads different metric name.

oncall-leah: hypothesis: router sees no capacity (ghost signal) -> fallback policy activates -> tries alternate variants/regions -> fallback route group has zero capacity or worse a bad mapping -> traffic gets blackholed -> customers see 502s.

incident-bot: @here Escalation level 2: on-call lead requested.

omar: quick mitigation: disable fallback policy for that route so router won't attempt cross-variant fallbacks. Command (APIs):
```
POST /admin/routes/v1/disable_fallback
{"route": "/v1/generate", "pool": "dedicated-us-west-2", "reason": "emergency - disable fallback until healthchecks fixed"}
```

priya: applied disable_fallback -> response 200. confirmed router is no longer trying fallback mappings.

jensen: next: we need to restore pool capacity. manual scale up to 12 nodes and hold autoscaler.

rui: running: `redwoodctl pools scale --pool dedicated-us-west-2 --replicas 12 --reason "incident manual scale"`

maya: also patching autoscaler to ignore alias metric for 30m: `kubectl patch cm autoscaler-config -p '{"data":{"metric_name":"gpu_free_slots"}}'` (previewing).

oncall-leah: customer impact: two mid-market customers reported increased error rates and timeouts between 15:02-15:24 UTC. Support notified, incident-ops channel copied. tagging for SLA review.

omar: verifying effects: after scale-up, active_workers rising to 11 by 15:10; 502s drop to baseline but latency slightly higher due to warmup.

priya: root cause: rollout 03:45 UTC changed metric names in telemetry pipeline. autoscaler config still referenced the old name and evaluated absent metric as value 0 -> triggered scale-down. router health check logic interprets zero as no capacity and triggers fallback. combined with a recent routing policy change that included an empty fallback group for that pool caused an accidental traffic sink.

jensen: action items now: 1) revert autoscaler metric name to historical alias + add validation in config; 2) fix routing policy to never point fallback to empty group (validate at deploy time); 3) add circuit-breaker so router won't blindly fallback to other variants when health=unknown; 4) postmortem.

rui: patch 1 already rolled: autoscaler now reads `gpu_free_slots` and we added `metrics_present` check. patch id: deploy-2026-04-23-rc3.

maya: routing policy patch in review, adding schema validation.

oncall-leah: timeline notes for postmortem:
- 15:01 autoscaler scaled down pool due to missing metric alias
- 15:02 router fallback engaged, attempted variant reroutes -> no healthy backends
- 15:02-15:24 customers saw increased 502s and timeouts
- 15:06 mitigation: disabled fallback policy for route /v1/generate
- 15:08 manual scale-up requested
- 15:10 pool stabilized, error rate returned to baseline by 15:24

incident-bot: Pager resolved: INCIDENT INC-2026-0423 moved to "mitigated" by oncall-leah.

jensen: I'm going to own the follow-up on routing policy validation. assigning to @jensen.

oncall-leah: I'll own the postmortem doc and customer impact notes, will draft and loop infra/sre. handing off to day oncall @sre-rotations.

sre-rotations: ack. will take next steps and coordinate with support for customer communication.

priya: small ask: add automated test to deployment pipeline that fails if routing fallback group is empty. saved a cluster-wide outage here.

omar: also recommend a short-term alert: if autoscaler acts on missing metric (metric fetch==null) -> send high-priority alert instead of immediate scale action.

rui: logging note: we saw `metric: null` events in prometheus exporter between 03:30-04:15 UTC after the rollout. we will keep retention of those logs for 7 days for audit.

maya: final check: I've re-enabled fallback in staging with schema validation; will not reenable in prod until postmortem and tests added.

oncall-leah: incident closed to mitigated state. please add anything else to thread. good job everyone. :thumbsup:
